what: D.R. Horton is the largest homebuilder in the United States by number of homes sold. It builds in 128 markets across 38 states, mostly entry-level and first move-up homes, and also owns a mortgage and title business and a majority of the rental company Forestar.
customers: First-time and move-up home buyers across the southern and western United States.
money: homes sold, weighted to entry-level price points
mortgage origination and title insurance for its own buyers
single-family rental communities and residential land development
moat: Scale that lowers its cost per home below smaller builders, and land positions bought through options rather than owned outright, which keeps capital light.
risks: High mortgage rates have slowed sales and forced price incentives
Buying down mortgage rates for buyers eats into gross margin
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 10% with a strong balance sheet
It builds the cheapest homes in a market with a long-term shortage of them
Lower mortgage rates would quickly revive demand
watch: Net sales orders and the gross margin after incentives.
